hero.title: Tilt sensor. Low precision. ±1° accuracy.
hero.description: The H310-TS100L brings ±1° accuracy to cost-conscious tilt-monitoring projects covering outdoor light poles, warehouse racks up to 8 m and automated-storage structures. Record an installation baseline and asset ID for each point, then follow posture changes alongside routine inspections. Choose this grade where its accuracy matches the angle changes your team needs to review.

operatingProfile.title: Three grades. One clear choice.

faqHeading.title: Frequently asked questions.
faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for selecting and installing the H310-TS100L low precision tilt sensor.

faqs.question: What is the H310-TS100L tilt sensor?
paragraphs: H310-TS100L is Hitelecom’s low-precision tilt sensor with ±1° accuracy, positioned for cost-conscious basic inclination monitoring across multiple fixed assets.

Applications include outdoor light poles, conventional warehouse racks up to 8 m, automated-storage rack structures and fixed equipment supports. Record each asset’s installation reference and compare later posture changes with its inspection history.

faqs.question: What does ±1° accuracy mean?
paragraphs: The ±1° value is the accuracy grade for H310-TS100L under the applicable measurement conditions. It does not by itself specify the smallest detectable change, a configured alarm level or the operating range.

Define the angle changes meaningful to the asset group, then match the accuracy grade to that inspection objective. Keep the mounting, reference and loading conditions consistent when comparing later readings.

faqs.question: When should I choose low, medium or high precision?
paragraphs: Choose H310-TS100L where economical coverage across many assets and the required inclination performance fit ±1° accuracy. H310-TS150M is the ±0.1° medium-precision option, and the existing high-precision entry is identified as 0.01°.
Use the meaningful angle change, point count and measurement conditions to select the grade. Tasks needing finer structural rotation measurements should be matched to a finer measurement grade.

faqs.question: Why choose a cost-effective grade for a multi-point project?
paragraphs: A project may prioritise basic posture coverage across many poles, rack rows or equipment frames. H310-TS100L is positioned for this cost-conscious use where ±1° accuracy matches the required angle-change visibility.

Give every point an asset ID, location and installation reference. This helps the inspection team locate changed readings and organise follow-up across the asset inventory. Quantities and the required supplied configuration form the project quotation.

faqs.question: How can it support tilt checks on outdoor light poles?
paragraphs: Record an initial inclination and pole ID for each selected lighting column. Later readings can be compared with that reference and reviewed alongside service visits, reported vehicle contact or nearby works.

Use a rigid approved fixing on the pole, clear of maintenance openings and electrical access. Include the mounting exposure, access arrangements and number of poles in the project plan so the supplied configuration fits the installation.

faqs.question: Which racks are included in the up-to-8-m segment?
paragraphs: The conventional-rack applications cover pallet, drive-in, cantilever and mobile pallet racking up to 8 m high. Identify each point by aisle, bay and upright so the angle record leads to a specific place in the warehouse.

Use the actual rack layout, loading arrangement and meaningful angle changes to select the monitoring points and accuracy grade. The height segment describes the target application; the installation and inspection requirements still depend on the particular rack.

faqs.question: How does automated-storage monitoring differ from conventional racking?
paragraphs: Automated-storage applications follow the posture of selected fixed rack frames or uprights. Point IDs can include the row, level and frame so maintenance teams can locate a change within a large storage installation.

Use the project’s actual rack height; the up-to-8-m conventional-rack segment does not limit all automated-storage systems. This application records structural member inclination. Stacker-crane alignment, shuttle positioning and other precise equipment measurements use their specified instrumentation.

faqs.question: Does the 3° example set the sensor’s operating range?
paragraphs: The illustrated 0° reference, 3° later reading and +3° change show how an inclination reading can be compared with an earlier reference. These example values do not define the supplied working range.

The example also sets no alarm threshold or safe operating limit for a rack, pole or other asset. Choose the real angle-change objective and review condition for the project, then match them to the supplied specification.

faqs.question: What should be recorded during installation?
paragraphs: Record the sensor and asset IDs, rigid mounting position, angle convention and initial inclination. For rack rows or pole inventories, include the bay, column or location reference so a later change can be traced to the correct asset.

Use an attachment suited to handling exposure and maintenance access. Compare readings under documented reference conditions, and renew the baseline after remounting, relocating the asset or changing its support arrangement.

faqs.question: Can I connect it through a mobile network or local gateway?
paragraphs: Provide the required communication route, installation country, coverage and any existing receiver or gateway. Confirm the available radio configuration, protocol and interface for the supplied H310-TS100L.
Agree the report content and update schedule with the destination platform. Where a local gateway or LoRaWAN protocol is required, confirm compatibility explicitly before ordering.

faqs.question: What reporting, power and enclosure configuration should I choose?
paragraphs: Scheduled reporting is every 12 hours — two reports per day. The published service-life profile is five years with 12-hour reporting, subject to the supplied configuration and operating conditions.

The acquisition interval, power arrangement and event-reporting workflow are agreed separately for the supplied H310-TS100L. The high-precision model’s published figures are not this model’s confirmed specification.

faqs.question: What should I send for a low-precision tilt-sensor quotation?
paragraphs: Include H310-TS100L, installation country, asset types, quantities and target date. For racks, provide the height and layout; for poles or distributed equipment, provide the inventory and mounting arrangement. Describe the angle changes the team needs to review.

Add a mounting photograph or drawing, the planned point count, update requirements and the destination interface. Include the intended inspection workflow and any existing system requirements so the proposal can be matched to the project.
